messages:
laura: FYI I created a migration doc to move 'timeouts & 429 fallbacks' out of the long runbook into a focused troubleshooting page. Draft PR at GH #6620. Need quick reviews on examples and a tiny Go snippet.

kevin: nice. can you list the exact change set here? I want to ensure we don't break internal runbook anchors that ops use in pager.

laura: plan: (1) add /docs/troubleshooting/timeout-429.md with short patterns: client timeout, server retry, context-trim; (2) update /docs/errors/429 to link to the new page; (3) move the UX guidance into a short callout box. I'll keep anchor names short (e.g., #context-trim).

priya: good. please include both sync and async Python examples + a Go example. Ops asked for a snippet that uses retry-after header parsing for 429.

laura: adding that. sample 429 handler I plan to include:

```
// pseudo-Go
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
if err != nil && isRateLimit(err) {
  wait := parseRetryAfter(resp.Header.Get("Retry-After"))
  time.Sleep(wait)
  // fallback: shorten prompt or route to cheaper model
}
```

kevin: add a note: parseRetryAfter can return 0 for malformed headers; prefer exponential backoff if header missing.

laura: good call. also adding a short JS fetch snippet showing client timeout + UI fallback.

tom: small editorial nit: in the old runbook we used the phrase "context-aware backoff". i think we should standardize on "context trim" in docs but keep a redirect note for older links.

priya: agree on standardizing. for SDK examples, can we use the retry header helper in our JS SDK? saves folks from parsing. If helper missing in Go, show manual parsing.

laura: noted. PR includes code comments calling out when to prefer client-side timeout (fast UI) vs server retry (better for idempotent ops).

docs-bot: docs CI started for PR 6620: linkcheck passed; snippet-lint flagged missing language on 1 snippet.

kevin: likely the pseudo-Go block needs ```go. i'll fix.

laura: fixed markup and pushed. also updated /internal/runbook index to point to new anchors; left the old runbook anchor as an HTML redirect.

priya: I rebased a small change to python async example to use asyncio.wait_for instead of manual timeout loop. shows best practice.

laura: pushed mergeable after priya's tweak. can we get one quick content + SDK review?

kevin: doing quick pass. two tiny suggestions: change heading from "When you see a 429" to "Handling 429s" and add an example telemetry query snippet to measure token-trim frequency.

laura: added telemetry query (one-liner for our metrics system).

docs-bot: snippet-lint passed; spellcheck flagged "fallthrough" -> should be two words in guidance.

laura: fixed wording. merging now so marketing can pull the blurb.

priya: quick follow-up: can we add an example test case in our snippet test harness that asserts trimmed prompt still produces acceptable summary length? helps catch regressions.

laura: good idea. i'll add a smoke test in the PR after merge. thanks all. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
